Set the look of the whole table

Source: R/table_plan.R
plan_style.Rd

plan_style() gives the settings that belong to the whole table: its rules, font, row heights, padding and width, and the default look of the header and the body. The arguments keep the names rtftable(), as_rtftables() and rtf_table_style() give them. What a table has per column or per cell is another verb's — plan_columns(), plan_cell_style(), plan_col_header(), plan_blanks() — so this list is the whole of it.

Usage

plan_style(
  .plan,
  border = NULL,
  align_count_pct = NULL,
  font = NULL,
  font_size_half_points = NULL,
  row_height_twips = NULL,
  row_height_exact = NULL,
  header_row_height_twips = NULL,
  blank_row_height_twips = NULL,
  cell_padding_left_twips = NULL,
  cell_padding_right_twips = NULL,
  cell_padding_top_twips = NULL,
  cell_padding_bottom_twips = NULL,
  cell_valign = NULL,
  table_align = NULL,
  markup = NULL,
  blank_row_normalize = NULL,
  border_header = NULL,
  border_spanning = NULL,
  border_body = NULL,
  border_first_row = NULL,
  border_last_row = NULL,
  border_group = NULL,
  header_align = NULL,
  header_bold = NULL,
  header_italic = NULL,
  align = NULL,
  bold = NULL,
  italic = NULL,
  underline = NULL,
  table_width_twips = NULL,
  table_width_pct = NULL,
  table_width_pct_of_writable = NULL
)

Arguments

.plan

A table_plan().

border

The table's rules, rtftable()'s border: "tfl" (the clinical preset), "none", or an rtf_border() object. Given with the border_* zones below (in this call or another), the preset is the start and each zone is merged onto its zone side by side, as style_zone() merges: border = "tfl", border_last_row = rtf_border(bottom = TRUE) is the clinical rules with a rule under the last row. A side a zone leaves NULL keeps the preset's. A whole-table rtf_border() is expanded by rtftable() first and the zones merged onto that, the pages style_zone() gives. Given with the look fields (header_bold, align, ...), the preset's rules stay the table's, and so they do with border_group, which adds a rule under each group; with no border and no zone of the table's rows, the default "tfl" keeps its rules the same way.

align_count_pct

as_rtftables(align_count_pct = ): TRUE realigns "n (xx.x)" cells to one width before the pages are cut, or the name of another built-in cell format ("count_paren", ...).

font, font_size_half_points

The table's font family ("Arial"; a named vector gives one a script slot) and size in half-points. NULL takes the document's.

row_height_twips, row_height_exact, header_row_height_twips, blank_row_height_twips

The heights of the body rows, the header rows and the blank rows, in twips (1/1440 inch); row_height_exact = TRUE makes a height exact (clipped) rather than a minimum.

cell_padding_left_twips, cell_padding_right_twips

The cells' left and right padding, in twips.

cell_padding_top_twips, cell_padding_bottom_twips

The cells' top and bottom padding, in twips (rtftable()'s).

cell_valign

The cells' vertical alignment: "bottom" (default), "top" or "center".

table_align

Where the table sits across the page: "left" (default), "center" or "right".

markup, blank_row_normalize

rtftable()'s markup (the cell-text markup applied when the page is rendered, such as "script") and blank_row_normalize (how blank rows are normalised then).

border_header, border_spanning, border_body, border_first_row, border_last_row

The rules of one kind of row (the column header, a spanning header row, the body, its first and its last row), each an rtf_border(), by the names rtf_table_style() gives them.

border_group

An rtf_border() drawn under the last row of each row group, the groups plan_row_group()'s mode finds. A plan with no plan_row_group() has no groups, so nothing is drawn. NULL (the default) draws nothing, and the table is written exactly as before. It is one of the border_* zones, and goes with border as they do. The rule goes to the group's last body row, not to a blank row between groups, and a group cut by a page break has it under its real last row only, not at the break. The last row of a page takes border_last_row when that is given: it wins, and the group rule is not written on that row, so there is no double line. The table's final row ends the last group: with no border_last_row it takes the group rule like any other group's. A table with no groups, or one, changes nothing.

header_align, header_bold, header_italic

The whole header's default look, rtf_table_style()'s fields.

align, bold, italic, underline

The body's default look, rtf_table_style()'s fields. One column or one cell is plan_cell_style(). The flags (header_bold, header_italic, bold, italic, underline) mean what they mean there: only TRUE turns the look on, and any other value, NA included, is the same as FALSE (not an error, as row_height_exact = NA is). align and header_align must be "left", "center" or "right".

table_width_twips, table_width_pct, table_width_pct_of_writable

The table's width: in twips, as a percentage (0–100) or a fraction (0–1) of the writable page width. Give one; if table_width_twips is given with a percentage, the twips win, and given both percentages, table_width_pct wins (as in rtftable()).

Value

The plan, with one more layer.

See also

plan_verbs for every verb; rtftable() and rtf_table_style() for the settings in full.

Other plan verbs: plan_after(), plan_append(), plan_blanks(), plan_cell_style(), plan_cells(), plan_col_header(), plan_columns(), plan_compare(), plan_digits(), plan_empty(), plan_filter(), plan_footnotes(), plan_hide(), plan_labels(), plan_levels(), plan_listing(), plan_nest(), plan_paginate_cols(), plan_paginate_group(), plan_paginate_rows(), plan_row_group(), plan_sort(), plan_stat_groups(), plan_stub(), plan_titles(), plan_total()

Examples

tbl <- data.frame(
  Parameter = c("Subjects", "Age, mean (SD)", "Female, n (%)"),
  Placebo   = c("86", "75.2 (8.59)", "53 (61.6)"),
  Active    = c("84", "75.7 (8.29)", "50 (59.5)"))

# Minimal: the clinical rules (a rule over and under the header, none
# under the last row)
pages <- table_plan(tbl) |> plan_style(border = "tfl") |> plan_apply()
class(pages[[1]]$border)
#> [1] "rtf_table_border"

# A house style: Arial 9 pt, taller rows, the table centred at 80% of
# the page width, its counts and percentages lined up
pages <- table_plan(tbl) |>
  plan_style(border = "tfl", font = "Arial", font_size_half_points = 18,
             row_height_twips = 300, table_align = "center",
             table_width_pct = 80, align_count_pct = TRUE) |>
  plan_apply()
pages[[1]][c("font", "font_size_half_points", "row_height_twips",
             "table_align", "table_width_pct_of_writable")]
#> $font
#> [1] "Arial"
#> 
#> $font_size_half_points
#> [1] 18
#> 
#> $row_height_twips
#> [1] 300
#> 
#> $table_align
#> [1] "center"
#> 
#> $table_width_pct_of_writable
#> [1] 0.8
#>
